steps.text: In a medium glass or enamel lined sauce pan over high heat, combine oil, peppers, garlic, onion and salt; saute for 4 minutes. Add the water and cook for 20 minutes, stirring often. Remove from heat and allow mixture to cool to room temperature.
Transfer the mixture to a food processor and puree until smooth. With the processor running, slowly add the vinegar.
Pour into a sterilized jar with a tight lid. This sauce will keep for 6 months when stored in the refrigerator.

review.reviewBody: I really love this hot sauce but had to give it less than 5 stars because if I had made it precisely as instructed it wouldn't have been good. The first time I made this I nearly passed out because the vinegar was so overwhelming. I just halved the vinegar and it worked wonderfully for me. We make it all the time now and it's a staple in our kitchen. We eat it with eggs and potatoes, tacos... anything that needs a little kick. We even add it to beans when we are making refried beans. So good!

Very good, very easy to make. It's hot, but not too hot. I tripled the recipe, but still used the one cup of vinegar. I used jalapenos from my garden, and deseeded about half of them. I strained the sauce before jarring it. I got 6/12 oz jars, and 2/ half pint jars from the tripled recipe. I canned it in a hot water bath for 10 minutes. I plan to make this every fall! This recipe is from The Jalapeno Cafe website. Try their popper recipe if you still have jalapenos :)

A good base recipe, but agree with other commentors and used about half as much vinegar and added 2 tbsp sugar. Seemed a good balance. I also added the juice of 1 lime. I wanted a slightly chunkier sauce, more like sambal olek chili paste, so I cut water in half. That gave me the consistency I was looking for, but that's a personal preference. Finally, I went for a full on canning of these jars in a water bath canner so they would keep longer, so to compensate, I cut the time cooking the pepper/onion mix to 10 minutes.

When I made my version of this sauce I used these ingredients, plus 3 pablano peppers and about double the salt. My prep for this a bit different though because I'm not fond of the outer skins in my sauces. I foil wrapped the onion (sweet yellow) oil, & garlic together and roasted them on the grill, and grilled and bagged the peppers. When everything cooled to the touch, I peeled and stemmed the peppers, blended everything smooth and added the vinegar and salt to taste. Then canned it as I would pizza sauce. I am really happy with the roasted flavor, and the tanginess of the vinegar plus sweetness of the caramelized sweet onion.

Used 1lb of assorted red-hot peppers and I doubled all the other ingredients except the vinegar, simmered for 20 minutes uncovered to evaporate some of the water and then used a food processor. Came out great will be making another batch just waiting for more red peppers. Thanks.

I always plant 6 jalapeno plants in the spring since a 6 pack is only $1.25. By the end of the summer I have so many peppers I never knew what to do with them. I stumbled on this recipe and tried it for the first time. I loved it and I like the extra vinegar taste. I use this hot sauce on everything. I even look for things to cook just so I can use this sauce. So fresh tasting and purely jalapeno flavored. I am already on my 3rd batch this year and this one I am only using red jalapenos that have been on the plant so long that they turned red. I also have added some banana peppers to cut the heat a little on one batch which also worked out great. One other trick I tried from another recipe was to add one fresh (uncooked) jalapeno at the very end of the cooking prior to blending it just to give it an extra bright green color and fresh taste.

Edit 12/08/23 I've been making this recipe lately just the way the original recipe was posted. I also have canned quiet a few jars. Once the sauce sits a while the the vinegar mellows out the flavor is amazing!! ........................................................... (My original post from 2019) I add two Carolina Reapers and two Ghost Peppers to this recipe, two tablespoons sugar. I cut the vinegar by a third. I doubled the garlic added red pepper flakes, black pepper. This year I had some cilantro fixing to go bad so I added it..wow. added a splash of Fish Sauce also. I have been making this recipe for years now. It comes out awesome!!

This stuff tastes great compared to store bought. I changed the recipe to make a smaller batch and changed the amount of a few things put into the sauce. I went with 10 med/large peppers. Seeded 5 of them. I only used a 1/4 cup of rice wine vinegar (its what I had on hand and actually works very well). Everything else was pretty much the same. I did add a pinch of sugar.. not sure if that did anything. After tossing it in the blender for a few minutes I salted to taste and squeezed about a 1/3 of a lime to give it some tang. Not sure how some people strained this hot sauce.. when I was done it was perfect for consistency so if i put it on something it will not run off.. I like it.. good first run anyways.

I tried a double batch of this, following the ingredients list with addition of a few habaneros. I removed most of the seeds. I like some acidity and didn't tamper with the vinegar. Great tasting sauce. Hot enough, but lots of flavor.
The one variation I made was pulling out some caps and the bottle capper from my home brew kit. Instead of putting this into jars, I used heat-sterilized 12 ounce beer bottles (not screw necks). A double recipe doesn't quite fill a sixpack . . . though it does result in more fluid than the blender can hold. I'd rather pour hotsauce than spoon it, so the beer bottles are great. Plus it provides an excuse to go buy a sixpack of some new microbrew.

I've made this recipe a couple of times with peppers from the same two plants with wildly different results. I used a standard jalapeño and a mucho nacho jalapeño plant. The heat is directly related to your peppers and how you care for your plants! Stressed plants ( of any pepper variety) will produce hotter peppers. I got slack in my watering late in the season and subsequently the latest batch of sauce ( using an equal weight of peppers from each) is much hotter than the sauce I made early in the season with daily watering. This recipe is a rip on a big E recipe. The 1 cup of vinegar makes it RIGHT, but you must let it set for at least 2 weeks. Sure you can add sweetener and reduce vinegar if you plan to use immediately. Hope you find this helpful if making for the first time. My biggest recommendation is to let it Rest! 2 weeks, it's worth it!

This is great , yes , with some minor modifications . And why go to all the trouble of buying fresh jalapenos @ $3.29 a lb . , and then cooking everything ? We bought a 16 oz. jar of packed-in-water jalapenos , dumped it all in the blender , threw in about a TBL of dried minced onion, maybe a half tsp of supermarket minced garlic , a quick glug of more water , maybe a quarter cup of vinegar , half a tsp salt , 2 tsp of sugar .... let it spin on high for a couple of minutes ...... GOOD!!! This makes about 24 oz , perfect for that big empty cottage cheese container. My sensitive wife and kids mix it with mayo for a killer BLT . Make this. Yummy .

A good simple recipe - but cooking the vinegar down with the aromatics and peppers. It mellows out the harshness of the vinegar. I also ran it through a strainer to get rid of the pulp ( I like smooth hot sauce)
Love this recipe no need to alter thanks!
I just love it. I'm addicted
I substituted the jalapenos with sugar rush peach peppers and added in some fresh pineapple - sweet and hot!!
Husband loves it!!!! I finally found a jalepeno recipe he loves!!!!
I made the jalapeño version and it was great. Then I made a Fresno pepper version with apple cider vinegar. It was fantastic and very colorful.
Made the recipe exactly as stated and it is amazing. Spicy hot, and the perfect consistency for use. Gonna make more when I get to.
My family loves this sauce, the change I made was smoked the ingredients in the smoker, and add a few spices.
Love the simple ingredients...good stuff
